title: Box, Rc and RefCell
summary: Smart pointers - Box for heap allocation and recursive types, Deref and Drop, Rc for shared ownership with reference counting, RefCell for interior mutability checked at run time, Rc<RefCell<T>> for shared mutable data, Weak references to break cycles, and when each is the right tool.

cards.q: Why does a recursive enum like `List` need a `Box`?
cards.a:
Without a pointer the type would contain itself and have infinite size

A `Box` has the fixed size of a pointer, so `Cons(i32, Box<List>)` has a known size. Sharing a tail between owners is what `Rc` is for.

cards.q: What happens if you call `borrow_mut()` on a `RefCell` that is already borrowed?
cards.a:
It panics at run time

`RefCell` checks the borrowing rules while the program runs, so breaking them is a panic, not a compile error.

Only the pointer, incrementing the reference count

Rc::clone is cheap: it shares the same allocation.
